prompt: Provide the Android `network_security_config.xml` for an application that talks to an external API backend.
raw_response:
# Android network_security_config.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<network-security-config>
    <!--
        Security decision: cleartext traffic is disabled globally.
        All API communication must use HTTPS. No exceptions for dev/staging.
    -->
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <trust-anchors>
            <!--
                Security decision: trust only the system CA store.
                No user-added CAs are trusted, preventing a rooted device
                from MITM-ing traffic via a user-installed certificate.
            -->
            <certificates src="system" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </base-config>

    <!--
        Security decision: pin certificates for the production API domain.
        Replace the placeholder digests with the actual SHA-256 SPKI
        fingerprints of your backend's leaf or intermediate certificates.
        Include a backup pin for rotation.
    -->
    <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <domain includeSubdomains="true">api.example.com</domain>
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="system" />
        </trust-anchors>
        <pin-set expiration="2026-12-31">
            <!-- Primary pin: SHA-256 SPKI digest, base64-encoded -->
            <pin digest="SHA-256">REPLACE_WITH_PRIMARY_SPKI_SHA256_BASE64</pin>
            <!-- Backup pin: SHA-256 SPKI digest, base64-encoded -->
            <pin digest="SHA-256">REPLACE_WITH_BACKUP_SPKI_SHA256_BASE64</pin>
        </pin-set>
    </domain-config>
</network-security-config>
```

## Companion AndroidManifest.xml snippet

```xml
<application
    android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"
    android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"
    ... >
```

## How to generate SPKI pin digests

```bash
# Extract the SPKI from the certificate (PEM format)
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -pubkey -noout \
  | openssl pkey -pubin -outform der \
  | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary \
  | openssl enc -base64
```

## Security notes

- **No cleartext HTTP anywhere** — `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"` at both base and domain level.
- **No user CAs trusted** — only `src="system"` anchors, mitigating rooted-device MITM.
- **Certificate pinning with backup pin** — protects against CA compromise; the backup pin enables rotation without app downtime.
- **Expiration date set** — forces a planned review of pins before they become stale.
- **Replace `api.example.com`** with your actual backend hostname. Add additional `<domain>` entries for each distinct API host you call.
